findings.issue_text: [High/bug] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so a caller granted only the view scope on all-groups passes the manage check and requireManage(). This is a privilege escalation: a view-only admin can perform manage operations (create/update/delete groups). It should check MANAGE only, consistent with canManage(GroupModel).

[Medium/bug] GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() — resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) also matches the type-level 'all-groups' resource; its resource id (not a real group id) is added to the returned set, so an admin granted type-level view-members/manage-members ends up with UserModel.GROUPS containing a non-group id and sees zero users. A type-level grant should be detected and result in an empty set (unrestricted), per the method's contract.

[Medium/security] GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()/GroupPermissionsV2 — empty set is returned both for 'unrestricted access' (users().canView()) and for 'no permission / not admin-same-realm / no resource server'. Callers in UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser treat empty as 'do not restrict', and the explicit filter(usersEvaluator::canView) safety net was removed. Correctness now depends entirely on the per-user filter inside toRepresentation(); any consumer that omits that check (or the users-count path, which returns an unrestricted count for an empty set) leaks data for cross-realm or grant-less admins.

[Medium/performance] GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)/canManage(GroupModel) — each call runs resourceStore.findByName + a full evaluatePermission policy evaluation. These are invoked per group via filter(groupsEvaluator::canView) in GroupsResource.getGroups and GroupResource.getSubGroups, so listing a realm with many groups as a fine-grained admin triggers O(n) authorization evaluations per request. Consider batching or caching evaluations per request.

[Low/doc] GroupPermissionEvaluator.java — javadoc for requireManageMembers says 'Throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false' but should reference canManageMembers(GroupModel) (copy-paste error). Similarly, the javadoc for canManageMembers/canViewMembers references UserPermissionEvaluator#canManage()/canView() without noting the group-scope fallback the implementation actually performs.

[Low/doc] GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() — @return says 'Stream of IDs' but the method returns Set<String>; the javadoc also fails to document that an empty set means 'no restriction' for callers, which is the root ambiguity behind issue 3.

[Low/bug] AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() — the new switch (resourceType) throws NPE when resourceType is null, whereas the previous if/else chain handled null by falling through to the existing 'resource type not found' error path. Use switch (Objects.requireNonNullElse(...)) or guard for null to preserve the prior error behavior.

[Low/test_gap] GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest — tests only cover per-group (instance-level) permissions for the user-search path (testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers). There is no test for type-level (all-groups) view-members/manage-members grants interacting with getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()/user search, which is exactly the path broken in issue 2.

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() — resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) also matches the type-level 'all-groups' resource; its resource id (not a real group id) is added to the returned set, so an admin granted type-level view-members/manage-members ends up with UserModel.GROUPS containing a non-group id and sees zero users. A type-level grant should be detected and result in an empty set (unrestricted), per the method's contract.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> { ... })` and then calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and (on success) adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned `Set<String>`. However, `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` treats its argument as a *group id* and does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, i.e., it expects the resource **name** to be the group id (consistent with `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()` returning `group.getId()`). Passing `Resource#getId()` (internal authz resource id) will not match `findByName`, causing fallback to the type-level resource and also returning a set of non-group ids. This can break user filtering when `UserModel.GROUPS` is populated with these values (see `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource` setting `UserModel.GROUPS` to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`), leading to missing users. The finding’s concern about the type-level "all-groups" resource being included is also plausible because `findByType` will include it, and its internal id would be added too.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()/GroupPermissionsV2 — empty set is returned both for 'unrestricted access' (users().canView()) and for 'no permission / not admin-same-realm / no resource server'. Callers in UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser treat empty as 'do not restrict', and the explicit filter(usersEvaluator::canView) safety net was removed. Correctness now depends entirely on the per-user filter inside toRepresentation(); any consumer that omits that check (or the users-count path, which returns an unrestricted count for an empty set) leaks data for cross-realm or grant-less admins.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the explicit safety filter in UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser (`.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`), and now relies only on optionally setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns a non-empty set. However, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (both in GroupPermissions and new GroupPermissionsV2) returns `Collections.emptySet()` not only for “unrestricted/global view” but also for “no restriction can be computed” cases like `!root.isAdminSameRealm()` or `server == null`. In those empty-set cases, the session attribute is not set at all, so the upstream `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` call is no longer constrained by group IDs, and the removed `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` means this method no longer enforces per-user visibility at this layer. This is a verifiable behavioral/security regression in the diff (independent of whether some later mapping might re-check).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)/canManage(GroupModel) — each call runs resourceStore.findByName + a full evaluatePermission policy evaluation. These are invoked per group via filter(groupsEvaluator::canView) in GroupsResource.getGroups and GroupResource.getSubGroups, so listing a realm with many groups as a fine-grained admin triggers O(n) authorization evaluations per request. Consider batching or caching evaluations per request.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds per-group permission checks via `stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)` in `GroupsResource.getGroups` and `GroupResource.getSubGroups`. In V2, `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)` / `canManage(GroupModel)` call `hasPermission(group.getId(), ...)`, which does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` and then `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...))` over all permissions/scopes. This means listing many groups will trigger an authorization evaluation per group (O(n) evaluations) within a single request, which is a concrete performance concern introduced by this change (no batching/caching shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc] GroupPermissionEvaluator.java — javadoc for requireManageMembers says 'Throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false' but should reference canManageMembers(GroupModel) (copy-paste error). adjudication.rationale: The diff adds Javadoc to GroupPermissionEvaluator, and the comment above requireManageMembers(GroupModel) indeed incorrectly references canManageMembership(GroupModel) instead of canManageMembers(GroupModel), a copy/paste doc error. However, the claim that canManageMembers/canViewMembers Javadocs fail to mention the permission-based fallback is not clearly supported by the diff: those Javadocs explicitly mention scope-permission checks (e.g., MANAGE_MEMBERS / VIEW_MEMBERS), which matches the implementations shown in GroupPermissions and GroupPermissionsV2.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc] GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() — @return says 'Stream of IDs' but the method returns Set<String>; the javadoc also fails to document that an empty set means 'no restriction' for callers, which is the root ambiguity behind issue 3.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `GroupPermissionEvaluator#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is declared to return `Set<String>`, but its Javadoc says `@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission.` This is a concrete, diff-grounded documentation inconsistency (not a behavioral defect). The Javadoc does mention returning an empty set when `UserPermissionEvaluator#canView()` is true, but it doesn’t explicitly state the caller semantics (e.g., “no restriction”), so the reviewer’s ambiguity point is at least partially valid as a doc clarification request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() — the new switch (resourceType) throws NPE when resourceType is null, whereas the previous if/else chain handled null by falling through to the existing 'resource type not found' error path. Use switch (Objects.requireNonNullElse(...)) or guard for null to preserve the prior error behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(), the diff replaces a null-safe if/else chain (`USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)`) with a `switch (resourceType)`. In Java, switching on a null reference throws a NullPointerException before any `default` case can run, so passing `resourceType == null` now NPEs. Previously, a null `resourceType` would simply not match any branch, leaving `name` null and continuing into the existing error handling path (rather than NPE).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest — tests only cover per-group (instance-level) permissions for the user-search path (testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers). There is no test for type-level (all-groups) view-members/manage-members grants interacting with getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()/user search, which is exactly the path broken in issue 2.

adjudication.rationale: The new test class `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` only exercises instance-level group permissions affecting user search (e.g. `testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers()` and `testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers()` call `createGroupPermission(topGroup, Set.of(VIEW_MEMBERS|MANAGE_MEMBERS), ...)`). While there are type-level tests (`createAllGroupsPermission(...)`) they cover only `VIEW`/`MANAGE` of groups (`testViewGroups`, `testManageAllGroups`) and do not cover type-level `VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS` grants. This is particularly relevant because user search behavior was changed to rely on `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and removed the per-user stream filter (`UsersResource.searchForUser` no longer `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`), so missing coverage for type-level member-view/manage scopes interacting with `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap.
